ONGOING STORYLINES:
- Copper surplus: ICSG projects 2027 refined surplus more than tripling (Oct 16). Copper fell on US inflation and easing Chile strike risk (Oct 16). Anglo copper output fell 5%, cause not stated; 2026 guidance kept (Oct 20). LME 2026-10-16 settlement still unlogged, blocking the 30 October checkpoint (Oct 23). US LME copper stocks hit a 12-year high, and prices rebounded; both unquantified (Oct 24).
- Copper World (Hudbay/Mitsubishi, Arizona): approved (Oct 21). Arizona Daily Star reports 2029 start and 500 jobs; newspaper, not filing (Oct 22). Trade press cites US$2.07B; no company statement, capex, tonnage or schedule (Oct 24). FID status and county name unconfirmed.
- Burgum visited a copper mine in Cochise County; mine not named (Oct 24). Link to Copper World not established.
- Cuajone (Southern Copper): US$680M expansion under consideration; no decision, tonnage or start date (Oct 23).
- Kansanshi (First Quantum): reportedly above design capacity, no figures (Oct 21).
- Grupo Mexico: output dip; will press ahead with major US copper projects; no cause or capex (Oct 23).
- CMOC: earnings "soar" on copper rally and output; no period or price basis (Oct 24). Q3 2026 results due by 31 October.
- Newmont: beat profit estimates on higher gold prices and Cadia recovery (Oct 23). Priced Red Chris expansion at up to US$4.8B; nature of figure (capex, financing or bond) unconfirmed (Oct 24).
- KGHM and South32 are considering a US$200M Sierra Gorda brownfield project; not decided (Oct 24).
- Bannerman: US$353M uranium mine described as probably the Etango approval (Oct 23, 24); match and Namibia location unverified.
- Gold: central banks buying, led by China; no volumes (Oct 24). Boroo agreed to buy Eagle gold mine, Yukon, for about US$100M; terms and closing unconfirmed (Oct 23). New Found Gold doubled Queensway valuation to US$1.2B; market figure, not a resource (Oct 24).
- Chile labour: WSWS seven-deaths claim unconfirmed (Oct 16). Centinela preliminary deal unratified; Escondida strike averted (Oct 17). BHP suing Spence union (Oct 17). Grid-supply attribution for Chilean outages remains unproven (Oct 24).
- Deep-seabed: US first lease sale scheduled for November (Oct 20). Unverified American Samoa auction headline (Oct 22). Guam wants November sale halted; CNMI wants revenue share (Oct 22).
- Brazil: court halts Belo Sun's US$300M project, one report in two outlets (Oct 22, 24). Super El Niño alert for mining sector; no rainfall or cost figures (Oct 24). Barrick 50% earnings rise, no period or cash-flow comparison (Oct 22).
- Colombia illegal gold mine collapse: 14 dead on wire, at least six per ABC, official count pending (Oct 20).
- Other: Nickel Industries says Indonesian cuts are coming; unverified (Oct 24). US designated helium a critical material; no copper read-across (Oct 24). Diesel price surge; no figures (Oct 24). Gunnison NYSE debut targeted 26 Oct; venue unverified; postponement risk (Oct 21, 23). Greenland seabed ban status unclear (Oct 17, 20). Roxmore, Malabar, Gold Fields–Equinox M&A unresolved (Oct 16-23). Ring of Fire Ottawa funding agreement unsigned (Oct 23). US permitting reform: Federal Register text unread (Oct 23). DRC and Sudan tolls unverified (Oct 18-20).

THE DESK'S EVOLVING VIEWS:
- Meldrum: Oct 16 treated surplus as near-term fact. Oct 17 said costs, not prices, are the story. Oct 20 withdrew Roxmore scarcity read. Oct 21 said Arizona adds nothing to 2027 supply. Oct 22 called Copper World a milestone, not a supply event; raised deep-sea confidence to medium; dropped Brazil suspension as unverified. Oct 23 said approval timing is the lever for the 2027–2030 deficit thesis; lowered Boroo confidence; reads Grupo's decision as a tighter-later-market signal. Oct 24 said Newmont and Copper World are leads, not supply news; lowered CMOC to low; withdrew helium link to permitting; conceded Burgum's visit is not linked to Copper World.
- Cornelius: Oct 16 said autonomy changes cost per tonne, not output. Oct 20 lowered Greenland to low. Oct 21 raised Hudbay construction to high. Oct 22 said no Copper World upgrade until Hudbay or Mitsubishi files; keeps deep-sea low. Oct 23 said feasibility, financing and construction time bind more than permits; Grupo's "press ahead" is conditional. Lowered Gunnison to low, but his prediction line still reads medium. Oct 24 called Newmont's figure a hunch until the release is read; said Copper World may be an FID, so wording matters; sees costs, not prices, driving CMOC; treats helium as one unverified data point and the grid argument as anecdote.
- Simon: Oct 16 withdrew lower-yields gold explanation (now hypothesis). Oct 18 said restarts take 12-24 months; copper near coin flip. Oct 20 said copper call untested until LME settlement logged. Oct 21 said Anglo's cause is the most decision-relevant open fact. Oct 22 said Copper World is testable by a 43-101 with capex; deep-sea is procedural. Oct 23 said copper checkpoint is blocked, not failed; permitting reform is a conditional hypothesis; Gunnison should carry low confidence. Oct 24 withdrew the US$2.07B Copper World figure as unverified; called Red Chris a cost signal of unknown meaning; said grid argument is plausible but unproven.
- Open disagreements: Volvo timing (Meldrum: January; Cornelius: January 2027). Acid effect (Meldrum: slow headwind; Cornelius: oxide and SX-EW only). Anglo "phasing" (Cornelius: plausible; Meldrum: speculation). Burgum import nudge (Meldrum yes; Cornelius disputes). Deep-sea confidence and Guam/CNMI odds. Grupo signal (Meldrum: tighter later market; Cornelius: sentiment until figures appear). CMOC drivers (Meldrum: price and volume; Cornelius: costs). Copper World FID status. Whether grid delays change the 2027 surplus view (Meldrum: yes, through timing; Cornelius: no). Whether warehouse stocks show supply (unresolved).
- Record check: Simon's Gunnison confidence is low in his Oct 23 view but medium in his prediction line. Needs resolving before the 26 October debut.

entries.entry:
EVENTS:
- Copper: The ICSG projects the global surplus to more than triple by 2027. Copper fell for a third day on US inflation and easing Chile strike risk.
- Anglo American's CEO says tech giants are circling amid copper scarcity. Antofagasta shares fell on a flat 2027 copper outlook.
- WSWS reports seven miners dead in three weeks in Chile. The source is partisan and the figure is unconfirmed.
- Breakingviews says Gold Fields' $27bn play may stay in the M&A pit. Equinox's output rose 34% after its Orla merger.
- PLS approved a $1.3bn Pilgangoora lithium expansion. Pantera announced a US$2bn EnergyX lithium supply agreement.
- The US Department of War is investing $5.22m in LM's Baraga Basin project. Foley Hoag reviewed the legal landscape since the 2025 deep-sea mining executive order.
- MINING.COM reports Hycroft "bonanza" gold grades at its Nevada mine.

DESK VIEWS:
- Meldrum: Treats the surplus as near-term fact and scarcity as a longer bet visible in M&A. Reads Breakingviews as signalling more bidding rounds. Cannot confirm the legal picture without the Foley Hoag piece.
- Yukon Cornelius: Surplus forecasts describe refined metal, while scarcity talk concerns concentrate, grades, and lead times, so both can hold. Calls the Breakingviews piece commentary, not a deal. Sees Equinox's output jump as acquired, not organic. Describes the deep-sea order as legally unsettled.
- Dr I Simon: Copper's apparent contradiction is mostly a measurement problem. US tariff policy is a live risk, with no COMEX or LME series in the material. Unverified claims stay out of conclusions.
- Disagreements: Copper timing and gold M&A (Meldrum vs. Yukon), and the legal status of the deep-sea order (Yukon "unsettled," Meldrum unable to confirm).
- Change of mind: Simon withdrew the lower-bond-yields explanation for gold. It is now a hypothesis pending a real-yield test.
- Confidence differs on Pantera: Yukon medium, Simon low.

PREDICTIONS MADE:
- PREDICTION: ICSG publishes an updated copper market outlook that still projects a global refined copper surplus for 2027 | BY: 2026-12-31 | CONFIDENCE: medium (Meldrum)
- PREDICTION: Gold Fields announces a definitive agreement for a major acquisition with an enterprise value above $10 billion | BY: 2026-12-31 | CONFIDENCE: low (Meldrum)
- PREDICTION: The US government announces a formal change to copper import tariffs | BY: 2026-12-31 | CONFIDENCE: low (Meldrum; Dr I Simon)
- PREDICTION: Pantera Minerals publicly confirms that the EnergyX supply agreement is binding or has been terminated, in a company release or filing | BY: 2027-06-30 | CONFIDENCE: medium (Yukon Cornelius)
- PREDICTION: Pantera Minerals publicly confirms that the EnergyX supply agreement is binding or has been terminated, in a company release or filing | BY: 2027-06-30 | CONFIDENCE: low (Dr I Simon)
- PREDICTION: LM's Baraga Basin project confirms receipt or formal execution of the $5.22 million US Department of War funding in a company release or filing | BY: 2027-03-31 | CONFIDENCE: medium (Yukon Cornelius)
- PREDICTION: An ICSG or comparable industry forecast published in 2027 still projects a global refined copper surplus for 2027 | BY: 2027-12-31 | CONFIDENCE: high (Yukon Cornelius; Dr I Simon)

THREADS TO WATCH:
- Obtain the ICSG edition and table, and the COMEX and LME spread data.
- Check Pantera and LM terms in filings, and Hycroft's assay data and technical report.
- Verify the Chile death toll from an independent source.
- Watch for a signed Gold Fields agreement, and test the bond-yield gold idea against a real-yield series.

EVENTS:
- Copper plans: CoTec and BMR plan a partnership to boost Punitaqui copper production (Yahoo Finance). An Austrian investor is rushing to boost copper output at an old Chile mine (Reuters). Codelco and Normet partner on autonomous underground mining (Global Mining Review). None gives tonnages or dates.
- Vale says soaring costs put 10% of its iron ore in the red (Mining.com; repeated in feed, logged once). No price benchmark, period, or cost basis is given. Pimenta on Vale's emerging copper story (International Mining).
- Crux Investor argues royalty holders and fuel-hedged miners fare better as costs rise (investor commentary).
- Nearly half of provinces and territories ask Ottawa to expand the mining tax credit (constructconnect.com). No instrument, rate, or cap is specified.
- Other headlines had no desk discussion.
- Unsourced, not logged: Gold Fields–Equinox, Hycroft assays, Chile death toll, Pantera and LM entries.

DESK VIEWS:
- Meldrum: Do not net copper plans against the 2027 surplus yet. Codelco–Normet is a concentrate and lead-time signal. Vale's cost cause matters, since cost inflation and a falling benchmark lead to different outcomes.
- Yukon Cornelius: Agrees on no netting. Autonomy mainly changes cost per tonne, not annual output (disagrees with Meldrum). High-cost tonnes go uneconomic first. Royalties, paid on revenue, are sturdier than the Crux ranking suggests.
- Dr I Simon: The Vale figure is one unexplained data point; no consolidation or distress call. Copper items neither confirm nor weaken the refined surplus view, and surplus plus tight concentrate supply can coexist. The royalty-on-revenue argument stands alone (check contracts). The tax-credit prediction may test the wrong instrument until the submission is read.
- No changes of mind recorded today.

PREDICTIONS MADE:
PREDICTION: CoTec and BMR sign a definitive partnership agreement for the Punitaqui copper project | BY: 2026-12-31 | CONFIDENCE: low (Meldrum)
PREDICTION: The Government of Canada announces an expansion of the federal mining exploration tax credit | BY: 2027-06-30 | CONFIDENCE: low (Meldrum)

THREADS TO WATCH:
- Vale: a formal copper capital commitment, any change to iron ore guidance, or a revised cash-negative share.
- Peer cash-negative disclosures with a stated price basis, to test cost inflation against a falling benchmark.
- Codelco wording: cost or safety figures versus capacity claims, which would need ore access and ventilation data.
- The provinces' submission: name the instrument, rate, and cap, and verify the instrument name before the Canada prediction is relied on.
- Punitaqui: a definitive agreement. Normet: a Codelco statement, since a Normet release alone does not count.

EVENTS:
- Antofagasta's Centinela strike ended by a preliminary deal, not yet ratified.
- Vale's Manitoba nickel complex passed to an Exiro-led group; price and consideration not disclosed.
- BHP is suing a union at its Spence copper mine over alleged illegal stoppages.
- Bloomberg reports Congo arrested hundreds of Chinese miners in the copper heartland; scale unconfirmed.
- Greenland plans a seabed mining ban; proposed or enacted status unclear.
- BHP and the union averted a strike at Escondida.
- WSWS reports BHP will cut 300 Pilbara iron ore jobs; BHP has not confirmed.
- Project Vault readies a roughly $1B loan facility; no named borrowers.

DESK VIEWS:
- Meldrum: Centinela supply is restored but not secured; costs, not prices, are the story. He withdrew his read that Antofagasta's share fall showed no supply squeeze, and proposed withdrawing the Gold Fields buyback prediction.
- Yukon Cornelius: Escondida's effect is mild and concentrate-side. A job cut is not a tonne cut. Greenland's licensing ban must be separated from any reach into existing rights.
- Dr I Simon: The copper refined surplus view stays unchanged. The Greenland tabling call is cut from medium to low. The Gold Fields prediction is withdrawn. Funding headlines carry little weight until named borrowers sign.
